claims.text: DIA published solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, 'ADVANCED AEROSPACE WEAPON SYSTEM APPLICATIONS PROGRAM', as a Combined Synopsis/Solicitation on FedBizOpps, original posted date 18 August 2008, response date 05 September 2008 4:00pm Eastern, original archive date 31 October 2008. Set aside: Total Small Business. Classification Code 'B -- Special studies and analysis - not R&D'. NAICS 541330 Engineering Services, size standard $25 million. Issued by the Virginia Contracting Activity for 'engineering services in the Washington DC area'. 'One firm fixed price contract is anticipated to be awarded as a result of this' solicitation.

DIA Talking Paper U-973-09 states the RFP broke the work into twelve technical areas: Lift; Propulsion; Control; Armament (radio-frequency and directed-energy weapons); Spatial/temporal Translation; Signature Reduction; Materials; Configuration/structure; Power Generation; Human Effects (of advanced tech on operators); Human Interface (i.e. pilot controls); Technology Integration.

'DIA received only one bid, from Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), in response to the RFP. DIA determined that the proposal was responsive and the contract signed on 22 September 2008.' (DIA Talking Paper U-326-09, 02 January 2009)

DIA Info Memo U-10-2552 to USD(AT&L): 'The Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program was first sponsored in the Fiscal Year (FY) 2008 Defense Supplemental Appropriation Act by Senators Reid and Inouye with a $10 million add. The purpose of this congressional add was to investigate foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats from the present out to the next 40 years and to build an infrastructure to house a center of expertise on advanced aerospace technologies.'

Same memo: 'The FY 2010 Defense Appropriations Act included a $12 million add for the project. Twelve additional reports were produced and delivered.' Total across FY08 supplemental ($10M) and FY10 ($12M) = $22M.

AARO Historical Record Report Vol. I: 'At the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats to the United States.' and 'DIA established AAWSAP in 2009, which was also known [as] AATIP.'

USD(I) memorandum to the Deputy Secretary of Defense states plainly: 'The AAITP that SEN Reid refers to is officially the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Application Program (AAWSAP) contract managed by DIA. Its primary purpose is to investigate revolutionary advances in future aerospace technologies with emphasis on research of unconventional and revolutionary technologies. The sole bid for the contract was from Bigelow Aerospace Advance Space Studies located in Las Vegas, NV.'
Same USD(I) memo: 'The resulting contract was for multiple sub-contractors to perform unclassified research in 11 technical areas and deliver technical reports on those areas by July 31 2009.'

DIRD inside covers name the program 'Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' and reference an 'AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100'. The program manager's name is redacted under (b)(3) 10 USC 424 and (b)(6) throughout the release.

The solicitation was issued through the Virginia Contracting Activity (VCA), DIA's contracting arm, and coded 'B -- Special studies and analysis - not R&D' rather than as R&D. Combined with the Total Small Business set-aside on a $10M congressional add, this is a procurement structure that minimises public visibility: VCA awards are largely absent from public FPDS/USAspending data (confirmed: FPDS ATOM query for PIID HHM402-08-C-0072 returns an empty feed).

desc: AAWSAP is the official, contract-of-record name of the program the public knows as the Pentagon's secret UFO study, and it is the most completely documented UAP effort in the history of the United States government. It was conceived inside DIA's Defense Warning Office by Dr. James T. Lacatski, funded by roughly $22 million placed in the classified defense appropriation at the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid with Daniel Inouye and Ted Stevens, solicited publicly on 18 August 2008 as HHM402-08-R-0211 by the DIA Virginia Contracting Activity, and awarded on 22 September 2008 as firm-fixed-price contract HHM402-08-C-0072 to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, LLC of Las Vegas at a $10,000,000 base value with four option years running to 30 September 2013. Its stated objective, in DIA's own words, was 'to understand the physics and engineering of these applications as they apply to the foreign threat out to the far term, i.e., from now through the year 2050', across eleven technical areas: lift, propulsion, control, power generation, spatial/temporal translation, materials, configuration and structure, signature reduction, human interface, human effects, and armament. In practice the contractor built a UFO research enterprise: a Las Vegas SCIF, field investigation teams, a case database, a human physiological effects program, a 494-page Ten Month Report delivered in July 2009, and 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents surveying every known theoretical route to the observed flight performance. AARO's 2024 official history concedes the drift in one sentence — 'although investigating UFO/UAP was not specifically outlined in the contract's statement of work, the selected private sector organization conducted UFO research with the support of the DIA program manager.' The program was terminated in 2012. What it produced beyond the 38 released papers — Lacatski says more than 100 detailed reports — has never been released.

claims.text: AAWSAP was solicited as a combined synopsis/solicitation posted 18 August 2008 under solicitation number HHM402-08-R-0211 by the Defense Intelligence Agency's Virginia Contracting Activity, coded 'B -- Special studies and analysis - not R&D' under NAICS 541330, and 'solicited as a total small business set aside.'

The Statement of Objectives dated 18 July 2008 states: 'The objective of this program is to understand the physics and engineering of these applications as they apply to the foreign threat out to the far term, i.e., from now through the year 2050.'

The solicitation asked offerors to provide examples from the past seven years 'of having performed, as a prime contractor, the analysis, design, construction, and flight testing of high performance aircraft and/or satellites,' stating that 'Success in this program is dependent upon this capability and experience.'

An amendment to the solicitation changed DD Form 254 Block 13 from requiring a Top Secret Facility Clearance from the Defense Security Service prior to contract implementation to stating that the contractor 'WILL NOT BE REQUIRED TO HAVE A TOP SECRET FACILITY CLEARANCE ... PRIOR TO CONTRACT IMPLEMENTATION. HOWEVER, IT MUST BE OBTAINED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE DURING THE INITIAL YEAR OF THE CONTRACT.'

The statement of work provides that 'Any accountable property acquired by the contractor with government funds during the execution of this contract shall become government owned property' and 'must be inventoried and returned to the government not more than 60 days after the end of the contract.'
The statement of work provides that 'The work under this contract shall be performed at the Contractor's facility.'

Contract HHM402-08-C-0072 was awarded on 22 September 2008 to BIGELOW AEROSPACE ADVANCED SPACE STUDIES, LLC, 4640 S Eastern Ave, Las Vegas NV, CAGE 54JU7, DUNS 827037768, as a firm fixed price contract, with a total award amount of $21,948,810.00 recorded on the Standard Form 1449.

The award document records deliverable line items of status reports, a project management plan for tasks 3.a.1 through 3.a.12, research reports for the same tasks, a Comprehensive Integrated Threat Assessment, travel and other direct costs, with a base year of 22 September 2008 to 29 September 2009 and option-year line items running into 2010.

AARO states that 'Although investigating UFO/UAP was not specifically outlined in the contract's statement of work, the selected private sector organization conducted UFO research with the support of the DIA program manager,' including reviewing new and Project BLUE BOOK cases, operating debriefing and investigatory teams, and 'proposals to set up laboratories to examine any recovered UFO materials.'
AARO states that 'DIA did not seek, nor specifically authorize, this work though a DIA employee set up and managed the contract with the private sector organization.'

AARO states that on 24 June 2009 Senator Harry Reid wrote to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting that AAWSAP/AATIP be made a DoD Special Access Program, and that 'Deputy Secretary Lynn declined to do so based on the recommendation of then-Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, James R. Clapper, Jr., that such a designation was not justified.'

AARO states that 'AAWSAP/AATIP was terminated in 2012 upon the completion of its deliverables due to DIA and DoD concerns about the project,' and that afterwards 'its supporters unsuccessfully attempted to convince DHS to support a new version of this effort dubbed KONA BLUE.'

The DIA FOIA release file for AAWSAP includes Reid's 24 June 2009 special access program request letter to the Deputy Secretary of Defense, DIA talking papers prepared for Reid's January and May 2009 visits, and contract status briefings dated December 2008, May 2009 and August 2009.

The BAASS Ten Month Report, the Utah property investigation report, the AAWSAP personnel roster, and obligation-by-year funding data have never been officially released, and no contract closeout property inventory required by the statement of work appears in the released record.

dossier.denialPosture: AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report concedes the UFO research but characterises AAWSAP as an unauthorised drift from an authorised aerospace threat study, states that DIA 'did not seek, nor specifically authorize' the UFO work, that the deliverables were 'exploratory papers' that were 'never thoroughly peer reviewed,' and that AARO 'has yet to uncover any other substantive UAP case work conducted by AAWSAP/AATIP.'
dossier.narrative:
AAWSAP is the best-documented UAP effort in the history of the United States government, and the reason is mundane: it was a competed commercial-items procurement, so it left a paper trail that the Freedom of Information Act could reach.

The solicitation went up on FedBizOpps as a combined synopsis/solicitation on 18 August 2008 under number HHM402-08-R-0211, issued by DIA's Virginia Contracting Activity at Bolling AFB, with responses due 5 September 2008. It was coded B, 'Special studies and analysis - not R&D,' under NAICS 541330, Engineering Services, and it was 'solicited as a total small business set aside' with a size standard of twenty-five million dollars. The Statement of Objectives, dated 18 July 2008, is unambiguous about what was wanted: 'The objective of this program is to understand the physics and engineering of these applications as they apply to the foreign threat out to the far term, i.e., from now through the year 2050. Primary focus is on breakthrough technologies and applications that create discontinuities in currently evolving technology trends. The focus is not on extrapolations of current aerospace technology.' Twelve technical areas were named, covering lift, propulsion, control, power generation, spatial and temporal translation, materials, configuration and structure, signature reduction, human interface, human effects, armament including directed energy, and other peripheral areas.

The qualification language is the tell. Offerors were asked to 'provide examples, conducted within the past 7 years, of having performed, as a prime contractor, the analysis, design, construction, and flight testing of high performance aircraft and/or satellites,' with the note that 'Success in this program is dependent upon this capability and experience.' The government was not shopping for a literature review.

The award document, Standard Form 1449, records contract HHM402-08-C-0072, awarded 22 September 2008 to BIGELOW AEROSPACE ADVANCED SPACE STUDIES, LLC, 4640 S Eastern Ave, Las Vegas NV, CAGE 54JU7, DUNS 827037768, with a total award amount of $21,948,810.00 and a base year of 22 September 2008 to 29 September 2009 followed by option years. The solicitation had anticipated 'a base year of 12 months from date of award plus four (4) 12 month option years' running to 30 September 2013. Deliverable line items were status reports, a project management plan for tasks 3.a.1 through 3.a.12, research reports for the same tasks, a Comprehensive Integrated Threat Assessment, travel and other direct costs.

Three provisions in the statement of work matter more than the money. First, security: 'The contractor shall comply with the terms and conditions of the DD-254 BEFORE initiating any classified effort,' and 'Contractor shall provide a work facility (including unclassified information systems) with a Top Secret Facility Clearance granted by the Defense Security Service (DSS).' But an amendment posted with the solicitation changed DD Form 254 Block 13 from 'THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE REQUIRED TO HAVE A TOP SECRET FACILITY CLEARANCE GRANTED BY THE DEFENSE SECURITY SERVICE (DSS) PRIOR CONTRACT IMPLEMENTATION' to 'THE CONTRACTOR WILL NOT BE REQUIRED TO HAVE A TOP SECRET FACILITY CLEARANCE ... PRIOR TO CONTRACT IMPLEMENTATION. HOWEVER, IT MUST BE OBTAINED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE DURING THE INITIAL YEAR OF THE CONTRACT.' The facility-clearance bar was lowered before award.

Second, place of performance: 'The work under this contract shall be performed at the Contractor's facility.' Third, and most consequential for this board, property: 'Any accountable property acquired by the contractor with government funds during the execution of this contract shall become government owned property. ... This property must be inventoried and returned to the government not more than 60 days after the end of the contract.' There is, in the released file, no closeout inventory.

What the contractor actually did is not seriously in dispute, and AARO concedes it. AARO's Historical Record Report states: 'Although investigating UFO/UAP was not specifically outlined in the contract's statement of work, the selected private sector organization conducted UFO research with the support of the DIA program manager. This research included: reviewing new cases and much older Project BLUE BOOK cases, operating debriefing and investigatory teams, and proposals to set up laboratories to examine any recovered UFO materials.' AARO adds that 'DIA did not seek, nor specifically authorize, this work though a DIA employee set up and managed the contract with the private sector organization,' and that the effort also investigated an alleged hotspot of UAP and paranormal activity at a Utah property then owned by the head of the contractor.

The special access question is the hinge. AARO records that 'On 24 June 2009, Senator Reid sent a letter to then Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting that AAWSAP/AATIP be made a DoD Special Access Program. Deputy Secretary Lynn declined to do so based on the recommendation of then-Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, James R. Clapper, Jr., that such a designation was not justified.' That refusal is documented in the FOIA record alongside DIA talking papers prepared for Reid's visits to the Director of DIA in January and May 2009 and an eighteen-page packet presented to the Deputy Secretary in November 2009.

AARO's account and the contractor's account of what the programme produced differ by an order of magnitude. AARO says the contract 'produced exploratory papers addressing the 12 scientific areas tasked in the contract's statement of work' which 'were never thoroughly peer reviewed,' and that it 'has yet to uncover any other substantive UAP case work.' The releasable record contains thirty-seven of thirty-eight Defense Intelligence Reference Documents. What is not in the record is the 494-page BAASS Ten Month Report, the Utah ranch investigation report, the personnel roster, obligation-by-year funding data, and the balance of the material that the government programme manager has described as running past a hundred reports. Under this board's sourcing rule, AARO's characterisation is a Tier 2 record of what AARO said, not a Tier 1 record of what exists.
openQuestions: Whether the property inventory and return required within sixty days of contract end was ever performed, what was on it, and where that property is now. The statement of work made everything the contractor bought with government money government property.

The obligated funding by year. The Standard Form 1449 records a total award amount of $21,948,810.00, but the line-item prices are redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(4) and no year-by-year obligation data has been released.
The full deliverable inventory. Thirty-seven of thirty-eight DIRDs are public; the Ten Month Report, the Comprehensive Integrated Threat Assessment, and the monthly status reports are not.
Whether the Top Secret facility clearance the amended DD-254 required 'as soon as possible during the initial year of the contract' was ever granted, and on what date.
Who the DIA program manager's chain of command was, and what internal record exists of the decision not to stop the UFO work that AARO says DIA never authorised.
dossier.whatItIs: The Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program was a Defense Intelligence Agency effort solicited publicly on 18 August 2008 as HHM402-08-R-0211 by DIA's Virginia Contracting Activity and awarded on 22 September 2008 as firm-fixed-price contract HHM402-08-C-0072 to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, LLC of Las Vegas. Its stated objective was to understand the physics and engineering of breakthrough aerospace weapon system applications out to the year 2050 across twelve technical areas. It ran to 2012 and produced thirty-eight Defense Intelligence Reference Documents plus a much larger body of work that has never been released.
dossier.whyImplicated: AAWSAP is the only documented instance in the modern record of the United States government funding a private company to study the physics of observed anomalous flight performance, and its own procurement file shows the seams through which such work escapes normal visibility. The solicitation was posted as a total small business set-aside under a classification code meaning 'Special studies and analysis - not R&D,' place of performance was the contractor's own facility, and the Top Secret facility clearance requirement was formally amended so that it was not required prior to contract implementation. The statement of work provides that any accountable property the contractor acquires with government funds becomes government-owned property and must be inventoried and returned within sixty days of contract end - a custody provision whose closeout has never been publicly documented. Senator Harry Reid asked the Deputy Secretary of Defense to convert the effort into a special access program on 24 June 2009 and was refused. The unreleased output of this contract, which its own government manager has described as running to more than a hundred detailed reports, is the largest identified block of missing documentary material in the modern record.

entityInfo.desc: Document custody map for AAWSAP. The releasable record falls into six groups. (1) Procurement: solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 with its statement of work (SOW_Aerospace.pdf, 22 Aug 2008), the award document HHM402-08-C-0072 released as FOIA-00349-2018 (13 Oct 2022), the commercial-items order released as FOIA-00269-2018 (28 Jun 2023), and the FY10 option modification (2 Sep 2009). (2) Status briefings: DI_Brief_2008 (16 Dec 2008), DI_Brief_2009 (8 May 2009), Contract_Status_24Aug09, and an undated Contract_Status_Briefing. (3) The Reid file: three DIA talking papers (5 Jan 2009, 4 May 2009, 19 Nov 2009), the Reid briefing deck of 8 May 2009, and Reid's SAP request of 24 Jun 2009. (4) The SAP decision chain: deliverables review U-429-09-DWO-IM (30 Oct 2009), OUSDI_IM_on_AATIP_Final, DIA memo U-09-2660CE-IM (13 Nov 2009), and the 18-page packet presented to the Deputy Secretary of Defense (17 Nov 2009). (5) The transition file: DIA info memo U-10-2552CE-IM-ATL to USD(AT&L), released in draft and in a four-page final under FOIA-00255-2022. (6) The deliverables: 37 of 38 DIRDs, released individually and as a bulk archive, plus the 9 Jan 2018 DIA letter to the Senate Armed Services Committee that lists all 38 by title and author. What is NOT in the record: the BAASS Ten Month Report (leaked, never officially released), the Utah ranch investigation report (DIA reports no records), the 19 Jun 2007 Lacatski-to-Bigelow letter (DIA reports no records), the SECRET/NOFORN version of DIRD 37, obligation-by-year funding data, the AAWSAP personnel roster, and whatever comprises the 100-plus reports Lacatski describes.
